newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices end even to down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices end even to down.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended Monday's lightly traded session flat to down 1/4 point as players waited for the week's $4.8 billion new issue calendar to give the market direction.
"It's a little easier, but not a lot," one trader said. "It didn't follow contracts, and I'd say we are easier by 1/8, 1/4 in spots."
A municipal analyst said high-grade issues were quoted slightly lower at session's close. Dollar bonds ended down 1/8 to 1/4 point.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond ended down 20/32 at 97-13/32 to yield 6.83 percent as selling pressure followed last week's gains.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was down 26/32 at 116-15/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 20/32 at 110-19/32. The MOB spread was 188 ticks.
Monday's new issue action saw Lehman Brothers reprice $29.66 million Massachusetts Industrial Finance Agency revenue bonds for Worcester Polytechnic Institute. The top yield was 5.55 percent in 2027.
The offering is one of 63 negotiated deals scheduled this week, expected to total $2.7 billion. A $540 million Puerto Rico Public Building Authority deal through Smith Barney Inc tops the list.
On the competitive side, 89 sales totaling $2 billion are scheduled. A $225 million Virginia Housing Development Authority issue on Tuesday is expected to be the largest.

"Puerto Rico is one of the focuses, and you have a whole slew of competitive deals here too," one trader said. "It's a big week, so the buyers are going to tell us where the market is going this week."
